bibl.title: Review of deep learning: concepts, CNN architectures, challenges, applications, future directions

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: deep learning as a field - its concepts, network types, CNN architectures, named challenges, applications and computational substrate
span.quote: We review current challenges (limitations) of Deep Learning including lack of training data, Imbalanced Data, Interpretability of data, Uncertainty scaling, Catastrophic forgetting, Model compression, Overfitting, Vanishing gradient problem, Exploding Gradient Problem, and Underspecification.

span.label: whether one review can supply a full understanding of DL, against a review literature in which each paper covers a single aspect
span.quote: Despite it has been contributed several works reviewing the State-of-the-Art on DL, all of them only tackled one aspect of the DL, which leads to an overall lack of knowledge about it.

span.label: a holistic survey of DL with twelve named challenges and their proposed solutions, a CNN-architecture lineage from AlexNet to HRNet, and a declared search methodology
span.quote: We review current challenges (limitations) of Deep Learning including lack of training data, Imbalanced Data, Interpretability of data, Uncertainty scaling, Catastrophic forgetting, Model compression, Overfitting, Vanishing gradient problem, Exploding Gradient Problem, and Underspecification.

span.label: critique
span.quote: Despite it has been contributed several works reviewing the State-of-the-Art on DL, all of them only tackled one aspect of the DL, which leads to an overall lack of knowledge about it.

span.label: a field whose knowledge is fragmented across partial reviews, so that assembling a working understanding requires reading past the reviews
span.quote: Several published DL review papers have been presented in the last few years. However, all of them have only been addressed one side focusing on one application or topic such as the review of CNN architectures, DL for classification of plant diseases, DL for object detection, DL applications in medical image analysis, and etc. Although these reviews present good topics, they do not provide a full understanding of DL topics such as concepts, detailed research gaps, computational tools, and DL applications.

span.label: a literature survey with a declared search framework - named keyword strings, named publishers, and a stated year distribution over 300+ papers
span.term: a literature survey with a declared search framework - named keyword strings, named publishers, and a stated year distribution over 300+ papers
span.quote: We have reviewed more than 300 papers on various DL topics. There are 108 papers from the year 2020, 76 papers from the year 2019, and 48 papers from the year 2018. This indicates that this review focused on the latest publications in the field of DL.

span.label: back-propagation multiplies each layer's derivative down the network, so with a squashing activation like the sigmoid, N small derivatives multiplied together make the gradient decline exponentially - and the first layers, which recognise the essential elements of the input, are the ones that stop updating
span.quote: However, this weight updating may not occur in some cases due to a vanishingly small gradient, which in the worst case means that no extra training is possible and the neural network will stop completely.

span.label: incorporating new information into a trained model interferes with what it already learned; fine-tuning on only the new class leaves performance on the old classes unsuccessful, so continually renewed data forces retraining from scratch
span.quote: This is defined as incorporating new information into a plain DL model, made possible by interfering with the learned information. For instance, consider a case where there are 1000 types of flowers and a model is trained to classify these flowers, after which a new type of flower is introduced; if the model is fine-tuned only with this new class, its performance will become unsuccessful with the older classes.

span.label: pre-training transfers representations learned from the source distribution; where the source is natural images and the target is raw medical images the learned representation does not apply, so the transferred model performs no better than one trained from scratch
span.quote: Nevertheless, although TL enhances the accuracy of several tasks in the fields of pattern recognition and computer vision, there is an essential issue related to the source data type used by the TL as compared to the target dataset. For instance, enhancing the medical image classification performance of CNN models is achieved by training the models using the ImageNet dataset, which contains natural images. However, such natural images are completely dissimilar from the raw medical images, meaning that the model performance is not enhanced.

span.label: many parameter settings satisfy the training objective equally well, so the pipeline does not determine which one is chosen; small modifications force the model toward a completely different solution and hence different predictions in deployment
span.quote: It has been shown that small modifications can force a model towards a completely different solution as well as lead to different predictions in deployment domains.

span.label: the paper recommends transfer learning for scarce data and then reports that cross-domain TL does not significantly affect medical imaging performance - its own central recommendation carries a negative result three paragraphs later
span.quote: It has further been proven that TL from different domains does not significantly affect performance on medical imaging tasks, as lightweight models trained from scratch perform nearly as well as standard ImageNet-transferred models. Therefore, there exists scenarios in which using pre-trained models do not become an affordable solution.

span.label: `RL` is defined as representation learning in the introduction and used for reinforcement learning in the classification section; a reader carrying the first definition forward misreads the second
span.quote: DL techniques are classified into three major categories: unsupervised, partially supervised (semi-supervised) and supervised. Furthermore, deep reinforcement learning (DRL), also known as RL, is another type of learning technique, which is mostly considered to fall into the category of partially supervised (and occasionally unsupervised) learning techniques.

span.label: underspecification puts major constraints on the credibility of ML predictions and the proposed remedy - stress tests - requires already knowing how the model can fail
span.quote: One of them is to design “stress tests” to examine how good a model works on real-world data and to find out the possible issues. Nevertheless, this demands a reliable understanding of the process the model can work inaccurately.

span.label: CNN performance is greatly influenced by hyper-parameter selection, so any small change affects the result - which limits how much a reported architecture comparison can be attributed to architecture
span.quote: The CNN performance is greatly influenced by hyper-parameter selection. Any small change in the hyper-parameter values will affect the general CNN performance. Therefore, careful parameter selection is an extremely significant issue that should be considered during optimization scheme development.

span.label: labelling remains the binding constraint: crowdsourced workers cannot annotate medical or biological images, expert labelling is costly and slow, so producing the volume of labels deep networks need is called unfeasible
span.quote: It is difficult to acquire sufficient training data for DL models. For example, in medical imaging and environmental science, gathering labelled datasets is very costly. Moreover, the majority of the crowdsourcing workers are unable to make accurate notes on medical or biological images due to their lack of medical or biological knowledge. Thus, ML researchers often rely on field experts to label such images; however, this process is costly and time consuming. Therefore, producing the large volume of labels required to develop flourishing deep networks turns out to be unfeasible.

span.label: despite the stated transition toward semi-supervised and unsupervised learning, most current deep-learning models still use supervised learning - so the data constraint above is not being relieved
span.quote: Although ML slowly transitions to semi-supervised and unsupervised learning to manage practical data without the need for manual human labeling, many of the current deep-learning models utilize supervised learning.

span.label: the architecture of the mammalian visual cortex, carried into network design - the CNN's local receptive fields are presented as a simulation of cells that sense only small regions of a scene
span.quote: DL, a subset of ML (Fig. 2), is inspired by the information processing patterns found in the human brain. DL does not require any human-designed rules to operate; rather, it uses a large amount of data to map the given input to specific labels.

span.label: pre-trained representations carried from natural-image datasets into medical imaging, and the paper's own report that this particular transfer does not work
span.quote: Nevertheless, although TL enhances the accuracy of several tasks in the fields of pattern recognition and computer vision, there is an essential issue related to the source data type used by the TL as compared to the target dataset. For instance, enhancing the medical image classification performance of CNN models is achieved by training the models using the ImageNet dataset, which contains natural images. However, such natural images are completely dissimilar from the raw medical images, meaning that the model performance is not enhanced.

span.label: a declared corpus for the review - a stated floor on papers read and their distribution by year - so that 'we focused on recent work' is a number rather than a claim
span.note: eliminates: a review's coverage claim resting on the reviewers' sense of having read enough · outcome: held
span.quote: We have reviewed more than 300 papers on various DL topics. There are 108 papers from the year 2020, 76 papers from the year 2019, and 48 papers from the year 2018. This indicates that this review focused on the latest publications in the field of DL.

span.label: declared review objectives - list and define approaches, list architectures, present challenges, assess applications and computational approaches - fixed in advance of the reading
span.note: eliminates: a review whose scope is settled after the reading, by fixing the five objectives in advance
span.quote: The selected papers were analyzed and reviewed to (1) list and define the DL approaches and network types, (2) list and explain CNN architectures, (3) present the challenges of DL and suggest the alternate solutions, (4) assess the applications of DL, (5) assess computational approaches.

span.label: cross-domain transfer learning checked against models trained from scratch - the control that decides whether transfer contributed anything, run by others and reported here
span.note: eliminates: that the reported performance is owed to the pre-trained source domain rather than to the architecture and the target data - models trained from scratch are the comparison that decides it · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
span.quote: It has further been proven that TL from different domains does not significantly affect performance on medical imaging tasks, as lightweight models trained from scratch perform nearly as well as standard ImageNet-transferred models. Therefore, there exists scenarios in which using pre-trained models do not become an affordable solution.

span.label: representation learning
span.quote: Among the different ML algorithms, deep learning (DL) is very commonly employed in these applications. Another name for DL is representation learning (RL).

span.label: RL
span.quote: Among the different ML algorithms, deep learning (DL) is very commonly employed in these applications. Another name for DL is representation learning (RL).

span.label: deep reinforcement learning
span.quote: DL techniques are classified into three major categories: unsupervised, partially supervised (semi-supervised) and supervised. Furthermore, deep reinforcement learning (DRL), also known as RL, is another type of learning technique, which is mostly considered to fall into the category of partially supervised (and occasionally unsupervised) learning techniques.

span.label: DL
span.quote: DL, a subset of ML (Fig. 2), is inspired by the information processing patterns found in the human brain. DL does not require any human-designed rules to operate; rather, it uses a large amount of data to map the given input to specific labels.

span.label: ML
span.quote: DL, a subset of ML (Fig. 2), is inspired by the information processing patterns found in the human brain. DL does not require any human-designed rules to operate; rather, it uses a large amount of data to map the given input to specific labels.

span.label: TL
span.quote: Nevertheless, although TL enhances the accuracy of several tasks in the fields of pattern recognition and computer vision, there is an essential issue related to the source data type used by the TL as compared to the target dataset. For instance, enhancing the medical image classification performance of CNN models is achieved by training the models using the ImageNet dataset, which contains natural images. However, such natural images are completely dissimilar from the raw medical images, meaning that the model performance is not enhanced.

span.label: Same-domain TL
span.quote: Same-domain TL is an approach of using images that look similar to the target dataset for training. For example, using X-ray images of different chest diseases to train the model, then fine-tuning and training it on chest X-ray images for COVID-19 diagnosis.

span.label: underspecification
span.quote: In 2020, a team of computer scientists at Google has identified a new challenge called underspecification. ML models including DL models often show surprisingly poor behavior when they are tested in real-world applications such as computer vision, medical imaging, natural language processing, and medical genomics. The reason behind the weak performance is due to underspecification.

span.label: stress tests
span.quote: One of them is to design “stress tests” to examine how good a model works on real-world data and to find out the possible issues. Nevertheless, this demands a reliable understanding of the process the model can work inaccurately.

span.label: Sparse Connectivity
span.quote: Sparse Connectivity: Each neuron of a layer in FC neural networks links with all neurons in the following layer. By contrast, in CNNs, only a few weights are available between two adjacent layers. Thus, the number of required weights or connections is small, while the memory required to store these weights is also small; hence, this approach is memory-effective.

span.label: Weight Sharing
span.quote: Weight Sharing: There are no allocated weights between any two neurons of neighboring layers in CNN, as the whole weights operate with one and all pixels of the input matrix. Learning a single group of weights for the whole input will significantly decrease the required training time and various costs, as it is not necessary to learn additional weights for each neuron.

span.label: Dropout
span.quote: Dropout: This is a widely utilized technique for generalization. During each training epoch, neurons are randomly dropped. In doing this, the feature selection power is distributed equally across the whole group of neurons, as well as forcing the model to learn different independent features.

span.label: Dying ReLU
span.quote: Occasionally, a few significant issues may occur during the use of ReLU. For instance, consider an error back-propagation algorithm with a larger gradient flowing through it. Passing this gradient within the ReLU function will update the weights in a way that makes the neuron certainly not activated once more. This issue is referred to as “Dying ReLU”.

span.label: catastrophic forgetting
span.quote: ### Catastrophic forgetting This is defined as incorporating new information into a plain DL model, made possible by interfering with the learned information. For instance, consider a case where there are 1000 types of flowers and a model is trained to classify these flowers, after which a new type of flower is introduced; if the model is fine-tuned only with this new class, its performance will become unsuccessful with the older classes.

span.label: vanishing gradient problem
span.quote: However, this weight updating may not occur in some cases due to a vanishingly small gradient, which in the worst case means that no extra training is possible and the neural network will stop completely.

span.label: overfitting
span.quote: DL models have excessively high possibilities of resulting in data overfitting at the training stage due to the vast number of parameters involved, which are correlated in a complex manner. Such situations reduce the model’s ability to achieve good performance on the tested data.

span.label: black box
span.quote: Occasionally, DL techniques are analyzed to act as a black box. In fact, they are interpretable. The need for a method of interpreting DL, which is used to obtain the valuable motifs and patterns recognized by the network, is common in many fields, such as bioinformatics.

span.label: imbalanced
span.quote: Commonly, biological data tend to be imbalanced, as negative samples are much more numerous than positive ones. For example, compared to COVID-19-positive X-ray images, the volume of normal X-ray images is very large. It should be noted that undesirable results may be produced when training a DL model using imbalanced data.

span.label: hyper-parameter selection
span.quote: The CNN performance is greatly influenced by hyper-parameter selection. Any small change in the hyper-parameter values will affect the general CNN performance. Therefore, careful parameter selection is an extremely significant issue that should be considered during optimization scheme development.

span.label: lightweight models trained from scratch
span.quote: It has further been proven that TL from different domains does not significantly affect performance on medical imaging tasks, as lightweight models trained from scratch perform nearly as well as standard ImageNet-transferred models. Therefore, there exists scenarios in which using pre-trained models do not become an affordable solution.

span.label: RL - REPRESENTATION LEARNING. Given in the introduction as another name for deep learning itself
span.quote: Among the different ML algorithms, deep learning (DL) is very commonly employed in these applications. Another name for DL is representation learning (RL).

span.label: RL - REINFORCEMENT LEARNING. Given 16,670 characters later as another name for deep reinforcement learning, a distinct technique the same paper classifies separately. Neither definition acknowledges the other
span.quote: DL techniques are classified into three major categories: unsupervised, partially supervised (semi-supervised) and supervised.
